text:
jordan_sales: customers running the POC hit a networking blocker — private connectivity to our inference endpoint times out or TLS resets. POC started yesterday, now stuck. can we swarm? :eyes:
anya_se: ack, can you paste the root error they see? is it DNS failure, TCP connect, or TLS handshake?
sam_infra: from previous POCs this smells like split-horizon DNS or egress firewall/NAT port exhaustion.
jordan_sales: error from app logs: "POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -> TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure". no 4xx from our side, connection closes after ~200ms.
maria_networks: do they have a PrivateLink/Interface endpoint or are they hitting public egress? also which resolver are they using inside the app VPC?
anya_se: asked customer: they said they created a Route53 private hosted zone for redwood-inference.internal and associated with VPC, but they also have a corporate DNS forwarder that rewrites some records.
sam_infra: can they resolve the endpoint to an internal ENI IP? please run:
```
dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2
traceroute -n <resolved-ip>
```
maria_networks: also get openssl output to inspect SNI/cert chain:
```
openssl s_client -connect <resolved-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts
```
jordan_sales: customer ran dig and got two IPs: 10.1.45.12 and 10.1.60.9. traceroute shows hops stop inside on-prem firewall.
anya_se: ok firewall is likely dropping or performing TLS inspection. if there's a TLS intercept proxy, that can break our client cert-based mTLS or expect SNI. do they have active TLS inspection?
maria_networks: if TLS inspect is present, they need to whitelist the endpoint (no MITM). alternatively use a VPC endpoint (AWS interface endpoint) that bypasses the inspect path.
sam_infra: note: some customers have outbound NAT that SNATs all flows to a small pool and hits ephemeral port limits under load — causes weird resets. check NAT gateway metrics.
jordan_sales: the customer says they have an egress proxy with mutual TLS pinned to their CA. they can't disable. any workaround?
anya_se: two options: 1) set up an AWS Interface VPC Endpoint to our service (PrivateLink) so traffic stays in AWS network and avoids corp proxy; 2) provide a dedicated endpoint IP they can allow-list + cert chain that matches expected SNI so their proxy can forward pass-through. which is easier for them?
maria_networks: On the PrivateLink option we provide a service name they create an interface endpoint for; they create a route53 private alias pointing api.redwood-inference.internal -> com.amazonaws.vpce-xxxxx. This avoids public egress.
sam_infra: if they can't do PrivateLink, we can ask them to add a split-horizon exception: forward the record to our authoritative IP block and skip TLS inspect for that FQDN. but that requires networking change on their side.
jordan_sales: customer asked about certs — they saw incomplete chain in openssl and their proxy rejected it. do we have a full chain bundle?
anya_se: yes we serve a full chain normally, but some internal LB configs terminate TLS and reissue. ask customer to capture s_client -showcerts output and paste. sometimes their proxy only accepts certain CAs.
maria_networks: a quick probe: use curl --resolve to bypass DNS to check cert served per-IP:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.1.45.12 https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health
```
this shows whether SNI and cert chain match. if that succeeds but app still fails, it's an app-level TLS client config.
sam_infra: also watch for ALPN mismatch if they insist on HTTP/2-only proxies. our endpoint supports both h2 and http/1.1 — but some middleboxes break h2. force http/1.1 for testing: `curl --http1.1 ...`
jordan_sales: customer ran curl --resolve and got a cert chain that includes an intermediary signed by our CA, but their proxy still logs "unknown issuer".
anya_se: in that case they need to add our CA to proxy trust store or use PrivateLink. we'll escalate if they can't change trust store.
maria_networks: action items: I can send a PrivateLink service manifest and sample CloudFormation for them to create interface endpoint. @jordan_sales can you confirm they have permissions to create ENIs?
jordan_sales: they do, but want an estimate for time to set up and if there are cost implications.
maria_networks: setup is usually ~30-60 mins on their side. costs: per-hour ENI/endpoint charges (~$0.01-$0.02 per hour depending on region) plus data processing. I'll DM rough numbers.
sam_infra: while PrivateLink is being tested, request they capture tcpdump on host while reproducing and share pcap (redact IPs). can help confirm where reset comes from.
jordan_sales: I'll coordinate and get pcap + s_client output. follow-up: can we provide a short checklist for customer to try before PrivateLink?
anya_se: checklist (quick):
• verify dig returns internal IPs bound to expected ENIs
• curl --resolve to test cert chain + SNI
• openssl s_client to inspect certs and OCSP responses
• check proxy logs for TLS intercept and add exception for api.redwood-inference.internal
• check NAT gateway ephemeral ports under load
• try forcing http/1.1 to rule out h2 middlebox issues
maria_networks: I'll draft the PrivateLink manifest and share in this thread. if customer wants, we can schedule a 1:1 tech call to do the endpoint create with them.
deploy-bot: scheduled postmortem note created: "sales-poc-network-swarm-1796543210"
jordan_sales: thanks team — I'll collect artifacts and loop back. :heart:
